slides.title: Me-facts point at you
slides.text: Pim says some facts are me-facts. Your name, your school, where you live and your birthday are all me-facts. Together, they can point straight at you.

slides.title: Sort the postcards
slides.text: Pim sorts her postcards into two trays. Fun facts go in the Share tray. Me-facts go in the Keep Private tray.
steps: Keep private: a photo in school uniform
slides.alt: The sharing sort: cards to split into Share and Keep Private, from favorite animals to passphrases.

slides.title: Small facts can join up
slides.text: One fact alone may look harmless. Add two more, and the three together can point at one child. That is why me-facts stay private online.

slides.title: Games do not need me-facts
slides.text: Some games and sites ask for me-facts before you can play. A real game never needs your address to let you play. If a game asks, stop and tell a trusted adult.

words.means: only for you and the trusted adults who look after you
facts about you, like your name, school or birthday
to show or give something to other people
something that is true about a person or a thing

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather, choose the Online topic, and play Online: share or keep. For each choice, ask: could this point at me?
